posts.body_html:
Your Iris verna is very stunning Mike.
I have Iris chrysographes now for nearly a century in my several bogs. Seedgrown so I have different clones.
forum.garten-pur.de/index.php?action=dlattach;topic=24435.0;attach=851886;image
Two other small Irises with big flowers grow well together with Sarracenia here.
Iris setosa var nana and now Iris hookeri which is close to setosa. This in the first year from seed.
Seeds of the true form I had from Canada.
The Iris setosa is very easy and grows even in a normal flower bed.


The Irises from Japan are stunning but I find them too big for my floating Islands. The cooling effecct of these islands is a relief for heat intolerant plants. Even Meconopsis takes 35 centiggrades uncomplainingly.
www.srgc.org.uk/forum/index.php?topic=18726.75

Do you have seeds from your Iris verna Mike?
I have a seedpot of Iris chrysographes from two different black clones. Probably there will be no way to swap with the new regulations.
